newsitem.title: NORWAY: Transocean to sell some assets.
newsitem.headline: Transocean to sell some assets.

text.p: Transocean Offshore Inc. said on Monday that its board of directors had approved the divestiture of certain non-core assets within its drilling services line of business.

"The specific activities to be divested include platform drilling, workover and maintenance, as well as engineering and construction services," the company said in a statement to the Oslo Stock Exchange.

The activities are performed by Transocean Petroleum Technology AS and Procon AS, both wholly-owned subsidiaries of Transocean ASA, and Transocean Engineering and Construction, a division of Transocean ASA. Transocean ASA is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Transocean Offshore Inc.

The company has retained Oslo-based Pareto Fonds to structure the divested business into a new corporate entity which will be sold to investors in Norway and subsequently listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange, the statement said.

Revenue generated from the business to be divested totaled approximately $110 million in 1996, including the period prior to consolidation with Transocean Offshore Inc. The divestiture is expected to be concluded within 90 days, Transocean said.
